clue.text: Horse seen by a short-story writer in a Japanese city

parts.note: a nag is an old or worn-out horse
Saki was the pen name of H. H. Munro, the Edwardian writer of short stories

explanation.surface: Someone spots a horse beside an author of short fiction while visiting Japan.
explanation.definitionFit: The port on Kyushu was the second city struck by an atomic bomb in 1945.

clue.text: Monster one observed in ascendant German city

indicators.note: one thing seen inside another sits within it, so the numeral goes into the city's name
in a down clue something rising is read from bottom to top, so the city's name is turned round

parts.note: Essen is an industrial city in the Ruhr
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A creature is spotted in a German city that is on the rise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ascendant' turns ESSEN into NESSE, and 'observed in' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The nickname of the creature said to live in Loch Ness in the Scottish Highlands.

clue.text: Where my amusing training may be seen?

definitions.text: Where my amusing training may be seen?

indicators.note: training licks something into a new shape, so these letters are reorganised

explanation.surface: A question about the venue where one's entertaining workouts can be watched.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of MY AMUSING rearrange to the answer, and the whole clue describes it too: a place where training goes on.
explanation.definitionFit: A gym is a hall equipped for physical exercise and training.

clue.text: Greeting to Roman healer

explanation.surface: A word of welcome is offered to a Roman doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: In Latin the word was used to say hail or hello; in English it is a soothing ointment that heals.

clue.text: Family doctor at home for most important person

parts.note: kin means one's relatives or family
GP stands for general practitioner, a family doctor in Britain
someone who is in is at home

explanation.surface: A family doctor who stays home is treated as the top person.
explanation.definitionFit: A key figure on whom an organisation depends, the central pin in bowling.

clue.text: Type of map providing I assistance

explanation.surface: A kind of map that offers help.
explanation.walkthrough: The page's stray 'I' is a scanning blemish; the clue is two definitions joined by 'providing'.
explanation.definitionFit: A map showing hills and valleys by shading or raised surfaces; also aid given to people in need.

clue.text: High-spirited bun eater managed to swallow ten

indicators.note: one part swallowing another takes it inside, so the numeral goes within the rearranged letters
managed is read as handled or arranged, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: X is the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.surface: A lively person eating buns manages to gulp down ten of them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'managed' rearranges BUN EATER into EUBERANT, and 'to swallow' puts X inside after the first E.
explanation.definitionFit: Full of energy and cheerful enthusiasm; a synonym for lively and buoyant.

clue.text: A playwright starts to introduce boring scenes expressing nothing

indicators.note: the starts of the following words are their opening letters

explanation.surface: A dramatist starts bringing in dull scenes that say nothing at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Henrik Ibsen was the Norwegian dramatist who wrote A Doll's House and Hedda Gabler.

clue.text: Preparing letters for the post, girl goes to royal male

parts.note: Fran is a girl's name, short for Frances
a king is a male monarch

explanation.surface: A girl takes her mail to the king to be sent.
explanation.definitionFit: Stamping mail with a mark that shows postage has been paid.

clue.text: Is a lemon pie a pudding?

indicators.note: in printing, pie is type that has been jumbled, so these letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a lemon pie counts as a dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pie' looks like part of the dessert but signals the anagram of IS A LEMON.
explanation.definitionFit: Semolina boiled in milk is a traditional British school dessert.

clue.text: Revolutionary article is on French land

indicators.note: something revolving turns round, so the whole string of pieces is read backwards

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
sur is the French word for on

explanation.surface: A revolutionary piece of writing appears concerning a French territory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' turns A + IS + SUR backwards as one run.
explanation.definitionFit: A country, the largest in the world by area.

clue.text: Man, say, in Paisley

indicators.note: the word in shows the answer sits inside the Scottish town's name

explanation.surface: A man, for instance, from the town of Paisley.
explanation.walkthrough: Man is the Isle of Man; 'say' marks it as an example. Paisley is a town near Glasgow.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Man in the Irish Sea is an example of an island.

clue.text: I deserve boiling

parts.note: to rate something is to merit or deserve it

explanation.surface: Someone claims they deserve to be boiled.
explanation.definitionFit: Boiling with rage means very angry.

clue.text: Author parking behind a king

parts.note: P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
astern means behind, at the back of a ship
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A writer leaves the car behind a monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Boris Pasternak was the Russian writer of Doctor Zhivago.

clue.text: Growth right outside church

indicators.note: one piece outside another wraps round it, so the legal word encloses the church

parts.note: a lien is a legal right to hold someone's property until a debt is paid

explanation.surface: Something grows just outside the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right' is not R here but a lien, a legal right.
explanation.definitionFit: A crusty organism of fungus and alga that grows on rocks and walls.

clue.text: Dishonest recreation for pleasure-seekers

indicators.note: re-creation means making again, so these letters are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: Dishonest pastimes appeal to those who chase pleasure.
explanation.definitionFit: People devoted to the pursuit of enjoyment above everything else.

clue.text: Unusual toenail yielding a sense of joy and pride

definitions.text: a sense of joy and pride

indicators.note: something unusual is out of its normal form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An odd toenail gives someone a feeling of delight and pride.
explanation.definitionFit: A feeling of great happiness and exhilaration.

clue.text: Rebel in south demanding immediate action

parts.note: S is the compass abbreviation for south
urgent means needing action at once

explanation.surface: A rebel in the south insists on action right now.
explanation.definitionFit: One who rises in revolt against established authority.

clue.text: Dotty, Sue, Pearl, Joy

indicators.note: dotty means crazy, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A list of names: Dotty, Sue, Pearl and Joy.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as four women's names; 'Dotty' is the anagram signal and 'Joy' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Delight or happiness, a synonym of enjoyment.

clue.text: An essayist sent back shameful letters

parts.note: Charles Lamb wrote the Essays of Elia

indicators.note: something sent back goes the other way, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: sad can mean deplorable or shameful, as in a sad state of affairs

explanation.surface: An essayist returns some disgraceful correspondence.
explanation.definitionFit: Lambda is the eleventh character of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Poker boss

explanation.surface: A card game and the person in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Stud is a form of poker; a stud is also a raised knob or boss on a surface.

clue.text: Dull-witted baronet plunged in river…

indicators.note: a thing plunged in another goes inside it, so the title goes into the river

parts.note: the Ouse is a river in Yorkshire and also one in Sussex

explanation.surface: A dim-witted aristocrat falls into a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Slow to understand; a synonym for dense or stupid.

clue.text: Former sweetheart enters punctually

indicators.note: one piece entering another goes inside it

parts.note: on time means punctually
the heart of the word sweet is its middle letter, E

explanation.surface: An old flame turns up exactly on time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sweetheart' means the middle of SWEET, not a lover.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-time champion is a past or erstwhile one.

clue.text: Jack was ill in prison

parts.note: J is the card abbreviation for jack
ailed means was unwell

explanation.surface: Jack fell sick while behind bars.
explanation.definitionFit: Locked up in a cell; the participle of a verb meaning imprison.

clue.text: … discovered coming by river is a hazardous activity

parts.note: an advent is an arrival or coming
the Ure is a river in North Yorkshire

explanation.surface: Following on from the previous clue, finding a way by river is dangerous.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis carries on from 21 across, where a river was also plunged into; here 'discovered' and 'by' act only as joining words, and 'coming' is a noun, an arrival.
explanation.definitionFit: An exciting and risky undertaking or exploit.

clue.text: Victor and Oscar get married, having made a solemn promise

parts.note: Victor is V in the NATO phonetic alphabet
Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet
to wed is to get married

explanation.surface: Victor and Oscar marry after exchanging vows.
explanation.definitionFit: Swore or pledged; a verb form of a solemn pledge.

clue.text: Polish scientist cut short before commencement of audience in papal court

indicators.note: a word cut short loses its last letter

parts.note: Marie Curie, born in Warsaw, discovered radium

indicators.note: the commencement of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A Polish scientist leaves early before an audience at the Vatican court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut short' takes the E off CURIE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman Curia is the administrative body through which the Pope governs the Church.

clue.text: Church leader has to update statement of belief

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: to redo is to do again, update

explanation.surface: The head of a church must revise its declaration of faith.
explanation.definitionFit: A creed: Latin for I believe, the opening word of the Creed.

clue.text: Imprudent university — one going in contrary directions

indicators.note: one piece going in another is put inside it

parts.note: northwest and southeast are opposite compass directions, NW and SE
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A rash university has someone heading two ways at once.
explanation.walkthrough: Northwest and southeast point opposite ways, which is why the clue calls them contrary; 'going in' puts the numeral between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking good sense or judgment; a synonym of foolish.

clue.text: Find agreeable place of torment? Not at all!

parts.note: to like something is to find it pleasant
hell is the place of eternal torment

explanation.surface: Asked whether they enjoy the inferno, someone answers no.
explanation.definitionFit: An emphatic refusal, informal for certainly not.

clue.text: First-born of Israel destined for central role?

indicators.note: the answer takes the central part of the phrase, its middle letters

explanation.surface: An Israeli firstborn seems destined to take a central part.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits in the middle of 'Israel destined', between ISRA and INED.
explanation.definitionFit: The oldest child of a family, the one born before the others.

clue.text: Doting doctors dote best

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so these letters are altered

explanation.surface: Fond doctors dote on their patients best.
explanation.definitionFit: Infatuated, so smitten as to be foolishly fond.
